items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: Yes, Mr. Hoss. Yes, Mr. Hoss.

ctx.x: So, uh, one day, I got out there then. Now, how it was, Frank Doosan had been out here, and they sent him back by not reading. And he said, here, he done sent the tickets to me on Lewis Armstrong, Johnny Dots, and Joe Lindsey. He's expecting. Of course, today, some fellas don't know that until today. I'm sure that happened now. I was going to get out. So, I had a ticket. I goes to Johnny Dots' house. Johnny Dots and his wife will accept me in. How to find him on a call. He had told his wife about it, but he had…

next to the ballroom. He goes with him and let's have a conversation over there. I don't know. I goes to his house. He didn't tell me. I noticed coming in a car, Louisiana Avenue car coming down. Now we come from Uptown to come see Dipper, get off at Petita and Rampart. I noticed he was kind of funny. He wouldn't say nothing. I said, well, he said, no, he wouldn't say nothing. So I said, well, I guess Dipper Rampart gets off. He goes down there, there's a little up in the place there, that ballroom there, a fella…

Like when you mentioned that, you know, things were getting too hot in New Orleans, so to speak, the cops breaking stuff up and everything. What was the attraction in California? I mean, why did California come to your mind rather than some other place outside New Orleans?
